sources.text: The American bison is a species of bison native to North America. By 1889 fewer than 1,000 remained in the U.S. Today they number about 31,000 in public herds. sources.title: Grace Hopper
sources.text: Grace Brewster Murray Hopper (1906–1992) was an American computer scientist and U.S. Navy rear admiral. She was one of the first programmers of the Harvard Mark I computer. In 1959 she helped design COBOL, a programming language for business. Rear Adm. Hopper retired from the Navy in 1986 at the age of 79. She is often credited with popularizing the term "debugging" after a moth was found in a relay.

sources.text: Australia is a country made up of the mainland of the Australian continent, Tasmania and many smaller islands. Its capital is Canberra, not Sydney, which is the largest city. sources.title: Ibuprofen
sources.text: Ibuprofen is a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug (NSAID) used to treat pain, fever and inflammation. The usual adult dose is 200 to 400 mg every 4 to 6 hours. Adults should not take more than 1,200 mg in 24 hours without a doctor's advice. Ibuprofen is not safe in the last three months of pregnancy. It can cause stomach bleeding, especially in people over 65. Dr. Stewart Adams and his team at Boots developed it in the 1960s.

items.reply: ANSWER: It was Doctor Stewart Adams at Boots. [1.6]

sources.title: Mount Rainier
sources.text: Mount Rainier is a large active stratovolcano in the Cascade Range of the Pacific Northwest. At 4,392 m (14,411 ft), it is the highest mountain in the U.S. state of Washington. The mountain is about 95 km southeast of Seattle. Mt. Rainier last erupted approx. 1,000 years ago, according to the U.S. Geological Survey. It is not considered dormant; it is listed as a Decade Volcano. About 3.7 million people live in the area at risk from lahars.
